security_spec.violation_condition: Kernel configures xsp as a dedicated interrupt stack (via MSECCFG.Smip enable) expecting hardware to cspspush/cspspop on interrupt entry/exit, but with cspspush/cspspop removed from ipush/ipopxret, interrupt frames land on the interrupted context's stack — if that context is near stack limit, the additional frame causes overflow; if that context is user space, the frame corrupts the user stack.
security_spec.summary: Removal of cspspush/cspspop from ipush/ipopxret means kernel must not rely on hardware stack-swap for interrupt isolation; interrupt frames always land on the interrupted context's stack

findings.finding: Only PMM (pointer masking) bits are defined for MSECCFG. No MIPU/SIPU (Smip enable) bit definitions exist. The kernel never writes to CSR_MSECCFG (0x747) — it only defines PMP-related read fields. The Smip control bits don't even have allocated encodings in the current RISC-V spec.
findings.snippet:
/* mseccfg bits */
#define MSECCFG_PMM			ENVCFG_PMM
#define MSECCFG_PMM_PMLEN_0		ENVCFG_PMM_PMLEN_0
#define MSECCFG_PMM_PMLEN_7		ENVCFG_PMM_PMLEN_7
#define MSECCFG_PMM_PMLEN_16		ENVCFG_PMM_PMLEN_16

spec_citations.excerpt: If 'MIPU', is set, a trap taken at Machine level due to an interrupt causes automatic stacking. If 'SIPU', is set, a trap taken at Supervisor level due to an interrupt causes automatic stacking. [...] NOTE: These bits do not yet have an allocated encoding.

findings.finding: Interrupt return uses standard sret, not sipopret/mipopret. The kernel does not rely on hardware cspspush/cspspop for stack management. Registers are saved/restored manually in handle_exception. No xspcs CSR is ever configured, so the conditional stack pointer swap path is never activated even if Smip were implemented in hardware.
findings.snippet:
csrw CSR_STATUS, a0
csrw CSR_EPC, a2
REG_L x1,  PT_RA(sp)
...
REG_L x2,  PT_SP(sp)
#ifdef CONFIG_RISCV_M_MODE
mret
#else
sret
#endif

spec_citations.excerpt: The existing trap behavior is modified. Before executing the first instruction of the trap handler, this extension ensures the interrupted context is partially saved. [...] It performs the following operations in order: Save registers x10-x15; Adjusts the stack pointer to create the stack frame; Conditionally performs a stack pointer swap by executing xcspspush sp

findings.finding: CSR_MSECCFG (0x747) and CSR_MSECCFGH (0x757) are defined but no kernel code writes to them. No xsp/mspcs/sspcs CSR definitions exist, and no cspspush/cspspop/scspspop/mcspspush instruction definitions exist. The entire Smip/Ssip instruction and CSR surface is absent from the kernel.

spec_citations.excerpt: mseccfg is a 64-bit read/write register, formatted as shown, that controls security features. It exists if any extension that adds a field to mseccfg is implemented. Otherwise, it is reserved.
